# Octo by OctoAI

> Desktop app, written in Rust, that runs and monitors multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Kilo, OpenCode, Antigravity, Grok Build, Qwen Code, Kimi Code and Pi) and plain terminals across multiple projects at once, organized into sessions, in one window. For Windows, Linux and macOS.

Octo shows every agent on a board by status (needs you, working, done, idle), with its project, time, type, a line saying what the agent is doing and the subagents that Claude Code and Codex spawn. The status comes from each agent's hooks, plugins and protocols, without relying on screen text.

## Highlights

- Alerts when an agent is waiting for you or finishes: chime, desktop notification, window title and alt+n to jump straight to the agent; ctrl+p pairs your phone, end-to-end encrypted, and `notify_command` sends the alert anywhere.
- One git worktree per agent (ctrl+t), on the `orkai/<name>` branch, with diff and merge.
- Plan usage (5-hour, weekly and monthly windows, or balance) for the agents you're logged into, with a countdown to the reset.
- Each agent runs in its own holder process: closing, crashing or updating Octo takes down no agent; after a reboot, ctrl+r resumes every conversation.
- Each agent's skills in the `/` autocomplete.
- Auto-update verified by size and SHA-256.

## Security

- Holders listen on 127.0.0.1 only, on a random port, with a 256-bit token per agent.
- Login tokens are read in memory only and sent, over HTTPS, solely to the service that issued them.
- No user config file is ever changed.
